newsitem.title: USA: Business must lead electronic commerce-US Treasury.
newsitem.headline: Business must lead electronic commerce-US Treasury.

text.p: The Treasury Department wants electronic commerce to develop with as few restrictions as possible and feels the private sector must lead the way, Treasury Under Secretary John Hawke said on Wednesdday.

"Innovation, expansion of services and participants and lower prices will depend on electronic payment systems and innovations remaining market driven, not operating as a regulated industry," Hawke said in a speech prepard for delivery to the Electronic Funds Transfer Association.
A text of his remarks was issued by Treasury.
He noted that many believe electronic payments -- using computers to settle accounts rather than cash and paper checks -- will revolutionize the global economy.

Hawke said there was "a paradox" in the U.S. payments system. Financial records have been computerized since the 1960s and securities markets rely on automated systems, yet consumer transactions largely use currency and checks.

In urging the private sector to lead in promoting broader use of electronic commerce, Hawke said any government action that is required should be predictable and mimimal rather than "top down regulation."
